title: Playwright vs Selenium: What Changed When I Moved 12 Scrapers Over
h1: Playwright vs Selenium: what changed when I moved 12 scrapers over
dek: Two years of running both against sites that did not want to be read. Where Playwright genuinely wins, where the difference is nothing, and the case where neither one helps.
description: Playwright vs Selenium compared on real scrapers: waits, session reuse, async, headless detection, and the one blocking problem no browser tool solves.
shareDescription: Waits, session reuse, async, headless detection — and the one blocking problem neither tool solves.

title: Why Your Scraper Gets Blocked (and What Actually Fixes It)
h1: Why your scraper gets blocked, and what actually fixes it
dek: Rotating user agents fixes almost nothing. A walk down the stack — IP, TLS fingerprint, browser signals, behaviour — with what each block looks like and what stopped it.
description: Why scrapers get blocked: TLS fingerprinting, IP reputation, headless detection and rate limits — the four layers, how to tell them apart, and the fix for each.
shareDescription: TLS fingerprints, IP reputation, headless detection, rate limits — how to tell which one is blocking you.

title: What a 429 Really Means: Retry Logic That Makes Things Worse
h1: What a 429 really means, and the retry logic that makes things worse
dek: The same status code covers "wait three seconds" and "this account is finished for the month". Treating them alike ended three runs early. The three-class taxonomy that fixed it.
description: HTTP 429 handling done properly: transient vs permanent vs exhausted, honouring Retry-After, and why substring matching on error messages breaks retries.
shareDescription: Transient, permanent, exhausted — three classes, one status code, and the retry loop that kept dying.

title: Local LLM vs API: The Numbers From Running Both on a 6GB GPU
h1: Local LLM vs API: the numbers from running both on a 6GB GPU
dek: A 7B model on a laptop GPU against a hosted 70B on a free tier. Four times slower, no daily cap, and one measurement that turned out to be answering a different question.
description: Local LLM vs API compared on the same task: what fits in 6GB VRAM, latency against Groq, constrained decoding, and when a free hosted tier is the wrong default.
shareDescription: 7B local vs hosted 70B on the same job: latency, VRAM sizing, quotas, and constrained decoding.

title: How to Test a Data Pipeline: 92 Passing Tests, 3 Broken Features
h1: How to test a data pipeline: 92 passing tests, 3 broken features
dek: A green suite proved the code did what it was written to do, and nothing about whether the product worked. What I test instead now, including the control run that has to come first.
description: How to test a data pipeline: why unit tests miss silent failures, measuring a source's noise floor before asserting correctness, and kill-and-resume scenario tests.
shareDescription: Why a green suite missed three live failures, and the tests that would have caught them.

title: A Year of Ingestion Bugs: What Actually Broke in 32 Data Pipelines
h1: A year of ingestion bugs: what actually broke in 32 data pipelines
dek: Roughly 30 bugs across a year of collecting Indian market data, sorted by cause. Eight of them produced no error message at all, and those are the ones worth reading about.
description: A year of data pipeline failures sorted by cause: bot blocks, silently wrong data, concurrency and config. What each one looked like and the guard that caught it.
shareDescription: Roughly 30 bugs across 32 pipelines, sorted by cause. Eight produced no error at all.

title: How to Scrape 20 Years of Data From a Site That Paginates by Date
h1: How to scrape 20 years of data from a site that paginates by date
dek: The endpoint only answers 180 days at a time, and the answers are not final. Windowing, deduplication that deleted rows, and why one source was never going to be enough.
description: Scraping a 20-year archive from a date-windowed endpoint: window sizing, resumable backfill, a dedup key that silently deleted rows, and handling a source that backfills late.
shareDescription: 180-day windows, a dedup key that silently deleted filings, and the indexing lag that forces a second source.

title: Why Rerunning a Pipeline Should Fix Data, Not Corrupt It
h1: Why rerunning a pipeline should fix data, not corrupt it
dek: A rerun is supposed to leave the dataset better than it found it. Four ways I broke that rule, the guard added for each, and the one case where it still is not guaranteed.
description: Idempotent, resumable ETL in practice: incremental loads, resume points that survive bad rows, anti-join deduplication, and reruns that heal gaps instead of corrupting history.
shareDescription: Incremental loads, adaptive backoff, and reruns that heal gaps instead of corrupting history.

title: Can You Predict Stock Prices Minute by Minute? What 9.4M Ticks Showed
h1: Can you predict stock prices minute by minute? What 9.4M ticks showed
dek: 61.4% right against a 46.8% baseline looks like an edge, until you notice it answered 70 times out of 3,100. The two ways I nearly convinced myself it worked.
description: Minute-level stock prediction on 9.4M NSE ticks: the baseline that matters, threshold tuning that leaks, sample size, and the backtest that settled it.
shareDescription: 61.4% precision against a 46.8% base rate — and why that was not an edge.
